effects: Moves NFT `tokenId` of this collection from `from` (the signer, or an owner who approved the signer) to `to`.
Clears the single-token approval on `tokenId` (_approve(address(0), tokenId) in _transfer).
Does not check that `to` can receive ERC721 tokens, so a contract recipient can lock the token.
formats.shown: "Transfer artwork" / "Transfer token <collection #id> from <from> to <to>", with From, To and the Artwork as fields.

effects: Calls onERC721Received on `to` when `to` is a contract, and reverts if `to` does not accept the token.
formats.shown: "Transfer artwork" / "Safely transfer token <collection #id> to <to>", with From, To and the Artwork as fields.

findings.title: safeTransferFrom interpolated intent omits `from`, which differs from the signer when an operator transfers.
findings.evidence: descriptor safeTransferFrom(address,address,uint256): interpolatedIntent "Safely transfer token {tokenId} to {to}"; sibling transferFrom uses "Transfer token {tokenId} from {from} to {to}". ERC721.safeTransferFrom allows any approved caller: require(_isApprovedOrOwner(_msgSender(), tokenId)). The From field shows the value.
findings.fix: Change interpolatedIntent to "Safely transfer token {tokenId} from {from} to {to}".

effects: Forwards `data` to onERC721Received on `to` when `to` is a contract. The data moves none of the signer's assets.
formats.shown: "Transfer artwork" / "Safely transfer token <collection #id> to <to>", with From, To and the Artwork as fields. `data` is not shown.

findings.title: safeTransferFrom with data: the interpolated intent omits `from`, which can differ from the signer.
findings.evidence: descriptor safeTransferFrom(address,address,uint256,bytes): interpolatedIntent "Safely transfer token {tokenId} to {to}". ERC721.safeTransferFrom: require(_isApprovedOrOwner(_msgSender(), tokenId)).
findings.fix: Change interpolatedIntent to "Safely transfer token {tokenId} from {from} to {to}".

findings.title: safeTransferFrom with data hides the `data` bytes passed to the recipient callback.
findings.evidence: ERC721._checkOnERC721Received: IERC721Receiver(to).onERC721Received(_msgSender(), from, tokenId, _data). The descriptor has no field for `data`.

effects: Lets `to` transfer NFT `tokenId` and replaces any earlier approved address for that token.
When `to` is the zero address, the call clears the approval on that token.
formats.shown: "Approve artwork transfer" / "Allow <to> to transfer token <collection #id>", with Operator and Artwork as fields.

findings.title: approve with the zero address revokes the approval but reads "Allow 0x0000… to transfer token".
findings.evidence: IERC721.approve doc: "approving the zero address clears previous approvals"; ERC721._approve sets _tokenApprovals[tokenId] = to. Descriptor field `to` is addressName with no special case for the zero address.
findings.fix: Add a label or message for the zero address on the `to` field, for example "None (revoke approval)", or say in the intent that the zero address revokes.

effects: When `approved` is true, lets `operator` transfer every token the signer holds in this collection, now and later.
When `approved` is false, revokes that right from `operator`.
formats.shown: "Set operator approval" / "true all tokens for <operator>", with Operator and a raw "Approved: true" field.

findings.title: setApprovalForAll shows `approved` as raw true/false, so the sentence reads "true all tokens for X".
findings.evidence: descriptor: interpolatedIntent "{approved} all tokens for {operator}", field approved format "raw"; case 4 renders "true all tokens for Test Operator". ERC721.setApprovalForAll: _operatorApprovals[_msgSender()][operator] = approved.
findings.fix: Map `approved` with an enum, for example true → "Grant" and false → "Revoke". Change the interpolatedIntent to "{approved} control of all your artworks to {operator}".

findings.title: setApprovalForAll intent "Set operator approval" does not say it gives control of all the signer's artworks.
findings.evidence: descriptor intent "Set operator approval". ERC721.setApprovalForAll lets the operator move any token of the owner (isApprovedForAll in _isApprovedOrOwner).
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Grant or revoke control of all artworks".

findings.title: setApprovalForAll tests only grant (true); the revoke path (false) is not tested.
findings.evidence: cases/4.json "Set operator approval - grant all" with approved = 1 is the only case for selector 0xa22cb465.
findings.fix: Add a test case with approved = false.

effects: Only the owner or the trustee can call it. It registers a new artwork with the title, the artist, the fingerprint and the edition size.
It moves no assets. Its artwork id is keccak256(fingerprint).
formats.shown: "Create artwork" with Title, Artist, Fingerprint and Edition size as fields.

effects: Only the owner or the trustee can call it. It sets the address that royaltyInfo returns as the royalty receiver for every token in the collection.
formats.shown: "Set royalty payout address" with the new Payout address.

effects: Only the owner or the trustee can call it. It changes the metadata base URI of every token. An empty string makes the contract fall back to "ipfs://".
formats.shown: "Set token base URI" with the Base URI string.

findings.title: setTokenBaseURI shows an empty base URI as blank, but the code then uses "ipfs://".
findings.evidence: FeralfileExhibitionV2.tokenURI: if (bytes(baseURI).length == 0) { baseURI = "ipfs://"; }. Field baseURI_ uses format raw.

effects: Only the owner or the trustee can call it. It replaces the IPFS CID of edition `tokenId`, which changes that token's metadata URI, and frees the old CID.
formats.shown: "Update edition IPFS CID" with the Artwork (collection #id) and the new IPFS CID.
